newsitem.title: USA: CSCE world sugar ends barely lower, rangebound.
newsitem.headline: CSCE world sugar ends barely lower, rangebound.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures closed a thinly traded session barely weaker, having climbed to resistance and failing to overcome the key level in earlier trade, floor sources said.
Most-active July settled off 0.01 cent at 10.79 cents a lb after trading from 10.86 to 10.78 cents. The outer contracts finished 0.01 to 0.05 cent weaker.
Volume was estimated at 6,797 lots, compared with Friday's official 26,606 lots.
Consumer buying lifted July to a high of 10.86 cents, the edge of resistance pegged at a gap between 10.86 and 10.92 cents.
Producer scale-up selling capped gains and knocked the contract off the highs and below unchanged by the close, dealers said.

They expect steady scale-up selling by producers and a heavy speculative net long position to remain obstacles to overcoming resistance and reaching the next overhead target seen at 11.00 cents in July.
Open interest in July stood at 75,644 lots, down 6,768 lots, as of early Friday.
At least one dealer said players are still digesting deliveries last week of nearly 360,000 tonnes.

"There is concern over whether the sugar will find a home and if it will open the door for more old-crop Brazil sugar to come on the market," a trader said. "There is still a lot of analyzing over the delivery."
A public holiday in London and Tokyo contributed to the dull tone in New York, floor sources said.
